operation_details.item: The user's Product A is in the beta phase.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hey, got a few minutes to chat through where things stand with the products?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Absolutely. I've been meaning to touch base. What's on your mind first?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Mostly trying to line up the next few sprints. Product A is currently in beta — I'm hoping we can wrap that up cleanly before we push more attention toward B.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Getting beta feedback on A while B is still in development will let you funnel any design lessons straight into the analytics add-on.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. And since both products share the same design system, changes on A should be pretty easy to carry over to B without a ton of rework.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That shared design system is a big win for speed. Are you seeing any particular friction in beta that you're worried might also show up in B?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Honestly, just the usual noise. The core flow feels solid. I'm more concerned about making sure the analytics add-on doesn't feel bolted on once B starts picking up momentum.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a fair concern. Keeping B's development phase aligned with the same design patterns should help it feel native rather than tacked on. Want to dig into any specifics?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Forget only the phase of Product A, while keeping Product B's phase, scope, and the shared design system.
